messages.body_plain:
Claudia and I will be giving a short presentation about GSoC next week at the UseR! meeting.

Could each "team" provide us with a short note on their project (we realize one stopped).
Suggestion:
 - one to two sentences on the aims of the project
 - one to two sentences on the progress
 - one sentence assessment (ie. things sometimes take different directions to the
   plans, but are still successful)

Does anyone think photos would be good? Other images? e.g., for optimgui we have some
screen shots, and I'm sure there are others.

We'll also be mentioning Mentors Summit etc.

And everyone should be aware of the Aug 15 "soft pencils down" and Aug 22 hard deadline,
with assessment to follow.

Best, JN

messages.body_plain:
The "Manipulating RStudio Graphics ..." project (GSOC student: Andrew Rich) is developing a series of interactive graphical applets, written using standard R graphics coupled to the new "manipulate" package, for teaching basic concepts in statistics and calculus.  As of the beginning of August 2011, the project has produced 20 such applets on subjects such as coverage by confidence intervals, Bayes rule, model term selection, differentiation and integration, and approximation of functions.  The project will be presented in a poster at the UseR! meeting next week.  (The draft poster, which contains screenshots of the apps, is available at http://db.tt/Nc5X5wq .)

-Danny Kaplan

messages.body_plain:
John and Claudia,

Here are some notes about the cranvastime project:

Project "Cranvastime" is developing interactive plots for temporal data, in association with a new interactive graphics
package for R named cranvas.

With the code currently written the plot can respond to several mouse events, like brushing, rescaling, and identifying points. With the rescaling, the time series can be wrapped on itself to explore the periodicity. The wrapping takes into account a time period variable, so it can be wrapped by unit (1), day (24), week (7),  or yearly (12) increments. Using a group variable, such as with longitudinal data, individual series can be vertically separated interactively.
Brushing can be done using a categorical variable, so that all data for an individual or group will be highlighted.
The cranvastime plot also responds to action on other cranvas plots.

The code is documented using Roxygen and will be ready to release when the cranvas package cis released. It works well on linux and Mac OS but the Windows binaries for the supporting libraries are yet to be built.

cheers,
Di

messages.body_plain:
Thanks.

FYI I built a new version of optimx with some of the sub-processes (KKT optimality check,
scale check and bounds check) in separate packages and Uwe's winbuilder hiccupped when I
wanted a Win binary. Turned out you need to upload and build the dependencies first (of
course!) unless they are on CRAN. I thought possibly it could not use non-CRAN
dependencies, but in fact is fairly "smart". Uwe had not documented this, so I proposed
some extra words (actually only a sentence -- all it needed) and he has put that in the
documentation now. Worked well, so possibly worth a try rather than struggling to load the
toolkit and mess with Win Environment variables. Never fun in my experience.

Best, JN

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Sorry for not replying earlier to this email. I have been away for a few
days and my internet connection is not good. PLease, find below the
answers to your questions. I also attached a plot of North Carolina
showing two areas of high incidence of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome in
children in North Carolina (from a test data set).

PROJECT TITLE: DClusterm: Model-based detection of disease clusters

> Suggestion:
> - one to two sentences on the aims of the project

Our objective is to develop a method to detect and evaluate disease
clusters in a spatial, temporal, and space-time setting that extends the
existing techniques and overcomes their limitations. To this end, we use
a flexible method that uses Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) and allows
the incorporation of information about covariates and random effects.

> - one to two sentences on the progress

So far we are developing the vignettes and testing the code to fix bugs.
We are also testing performance on computers with several CPUs.

> - one sentence assessment (ie. things sometimes take different
directions to the plans, but are still successful)

Not sure what you mean here... but we realised that by using GLM's this
package could be used for outcomes that are not Poisson or Binomial (as
it is the case in spatial epidemiology).
We are using ROxygen to document the code and package snowfall to be
able to make use of several CPUs.

Hope you can add some stuff on this project to your slides or comment it
in your presentation.

Best,

Virgilio

http://www.google-melange.com/gsoc/document/show/gsoc_program/google/gsoc2011/codeguidelines

is the description of the requirement that Google makes for code in the form of a tarball.

Can students please copy me (nas...@uottawa.ca) on this so I can use them to prepare the
blog item Google wants as well as the R-Journal report we will make? I realize most of you
have prepared vignettes and packages -- we "R" R after all! However, adding a cc is not a
big chore so Claudia and I can do the required reporting and ensure positive vibes for the
GSoC 2012 process.

If mentors have comments, feel free to send them too.

Best,

JN
